In the other direction, 48 census-captured entries are not usable fields; 39 of them sit only inside the args JSON string.
Gemini shell results: 445 of 1,419 (A+B) have text 'Exit Code: N' with N != 0, and 0 of those have native_error true.
61 of 96 Codex A+B sessions write no exec_command_end at all, so the exit code exists only in the output header text. 1,346 exited outputs have exit_code null, 85 of them with a nonzero header exit.

One Gemini session in A (d8bda4a8...) has no timestamp on any event (1,028 of 8,356 Gemini A events) and holds all 487 toolCalls without results. One Claude Code A session (6 events) is also fully untimed.
cc_local subagent events are stamped after their parent call's result in 113,950 of 114,045 cases (Workflow 111,625 / 111,664). Parent-child ordering is inverted by design (background runs).
In cc_local, tool_use.input differs from the harness wireToolInputs copy in 4,473 cases (equal 14,250); 4,072 of them are a stripped 'cd ... &&' prefix.
conversations.parquet lacks 38,178 raw call ids in the 2,200 sampled sessions, including all 10,923 Codex calls (the table has 0).

Claude Code native_error is filled on only 0.328 [0.285, 0.370] of swechat A results, 0.650 [0.394, 0.790] in cc_local and 0.178 [0.108, 0.247] in aiv_cc, because is_error is absent rather than false. exit_code is 0% for every Claude Code corpus.
aiv_cu: 613 model-generated mouse_move to (512,384), the bootstrap target, besides the 66,294 synthetic bootstrap turns; 27,752 executed actions matched no provider tool call.

No build or review report has a parser_surprises or open_problems field. The 80 items were compiled from counters and review checks in 14 of the 15 build files. All 25 cross-report same-fact checks agree. 5 review findings are already resolved in the current build.
The review-2 cc_local row counts (A 17,762) predate the current cache (A 21,222): thinking-only meta rows were added after the review, so review numbers cannot be compared to caches 1:1.

The rule set needed 8 corrections after the first run, 7 of them removing false name-level matches: nested toolUseResult keys, coarse AIV slices, joined-row verification, OpenCode messageID. Leaf-name matching against extra is unreliable without per-entry-type slicing.
implications_for_phase_b: The highest-fill redundancy fields, which make cross-record consistency checks possible, are all outside the IR today: Claude Code Read numLines vs text, Edit structuredPatch line counts, Grep/Glob counts, stop_hook_summary hookCount/hookInfos durationMs, assistant stop_reason, Gemini diffStat and tokens.thoughts/total, OpenCode reasoning/completion clocks and tokens.total, Codex last_token_usage.total_tokens. A Phase B mechanism that needs them requires a loader change, decided by day, before thresholds are set. Probes reading only the current IR cannot use them.

Do not treat a null native_error / exit_code as success. Fill varies by format: Claude Code is filled only when is_error is present; Gemini never flags a nonzero 'Exit Code' in text; 61 Codex sessions have no structured exit at all; aiv_cu has no failure flag. Stratify error-based probes by format, and use extra.marker / text headers only where documented.

Latency probes must account for: Claude Code (124,103) and OpenCode (6,662) out-of-order writes; cc_local background subagents running after their parent's result; aiv_cu latency only for Gemini, from 2025-12; variable fractional digits in AI Village created_at; Who&When and Cursor having no timestamps at all.
Use raw transcripts, not conversations.parquet. The table drops every Codex call and 27,156 Claude Code call ids in the sample.
Some surprise counts come from build reports computed on A+B or on full populations. They describe parser behaviour and must not be used to tune Phase B thresholds.

Session-level tallies (cc_local cost-state, OpenCode session summary, Copilot session.shutdown) live in entry types the loaders skip. A recount-vs-tally check would need those entries emitted (cost-state: 113 records in 111 of 332 main files).
could_not_measure: Whether the uncaptured fields agree with the IR (for example hook durations vs event gaps, or file-history backup versions vs Edit results). A6 is an inventory; agreement needs the raw fields, which the IR does not hold.

75 slice_absent_in_A entries and 121 inconclusive_rare entries: the entry type or field is too rare in the A sample to tell a loader drop from sampling absence. Examples are Codex turn_aborted duration_ms/reason, cc_local subagent attachments (subagent files are in 10 of 309 sessions; A holds 4) and swechat Claude Code async_hook_response.
Census-marked cc_jsonl paths (583 entries) were trusted from the census's code-derived path list, not re-verified as non-null in the A caches.
aiv_cu population fill from pass-1 stats has no session-clustered CI, because the pass-1 index carries no session ids. List-level paths count elements, not rows, so no rate is given for them.
AI Village tables outside the IR (events, chat_messages, agent_memories, ...) were censused only on their first 20,000 rows by the earlier agent. village-transcript.json was not censused at all.

The value equivalence of rule-mapped fields that live on another row was not checked. Examples: OpenCode message-level info.tokens vs step-finish usage, and Gemini functionResponse.id vs call id. Only presence was verified.

No build or review report contains parser_surprises or open_problems fields. The surprise list is a hand-selected compilation; every value is read from the reports at run time, but the selection itself is judgement.

overclaims: Fills are key presence presented as value fill. The a6 script never reads the census 'types' (null counts), and the IR inventory also counts keys, not non-null values. Affected: aiv_cc stop_reason '13792/13792' (non-null 126/77,716 in A, 14/13,792 in the census); aiv_cu Anthropic stop_sequence '907,506/907,506' (0/2,461 in A) and SDK stop_reason '11,679/11,679' (0/586 in A); swechat CC stop_reason '19457/19457' (non-null 5,191/17,932 = 0.290 in A raw) and stop_sequence (60/19,457 non-null); cc_local stop_sequence (10/8,640) and subagent stop_reason (4,133/13,048). At least 12 of the 435 'harness_measured, raw fill >= 0.3' candidates are majority-null or all-null: 7 by census types, plus 5 aiv_cu pass-1 stop_* entries that are null in A. These sit inside 'uncaptured' status: their expected non-null count in A is about 0, below the measurer's own threshold of 3.

'Read file.numLines 0.982 ... the A slice has 4,043 result rows' implies near-full coverage of the A slice. 1,794 of those rows are subagent results with the field on 6/1,794. Per-row availability in A is 2,180/4,042 = 0.539 [0.456, 0.634]. The same top-level-only fill is set against nested-inclusive A row counts in the 1.2 tables.

'The highest-fill redundancy fields ... are all outside the IR' and the linkage-id list: sourceToolAssistantUUID equals the IR parent_uuid on 9,338/9,340 swechat A results, so it is already captured. OpenCode info.finish equals the step-finish 'reason' that the IR keeps in extra.reason (3,227/3,227 A messages).
